translations.text: Of Shenoute.

During the night when we disciplined these ignorant men in the house of God, toward dawn on the [?] day of the month of Tobi, they were confined and bound, as we were about to judge those unclean people who were strangers to the place of Christ.
I considered this matter as I appealed to the Lord of all: whether it was right to leave them in these congregations, or whether their root should be torn out of them.

Look, a man assuming the appearance of authority, sent by someone greater than himself, pushed his way through the doors of those places without asking. Another followed him, as though he too were subordinate to this one.
He seized me as I was passing through the courtyards of these places, distressed over those pestilent men.
He began raising his hand against me and fighting with me, acting like someone looking after those people.
I resisted him in turn, so as to seize him by the object fastened to his neck or around his throat, saying these words: “I am not afraid at all, nor am I troubled about who you are.
What is the matter with you? Why do you hide yourself instead of revealing yourself?

If you are a spirit or an angel who has come from God, I too am his servant. And even if you stop, I will not stop. Or tell me whether you were sent because they are the ones who sinned against God, or because we are the ones who sinned against him by planning to remove them from our midst. Otherwise, we will not let you go, but I will fight against you even harder.”
While I was saying these things and others, he struggled with me, wanting to leave. I struggled with him and gained strength against him and over him.
And when he acted like someone who wanted to cry out, I struck him down on the ground.
I held his chest down with my feet while standing and calling to the brothers whom I could see around me, supporting me throughout this struggle: “Grab this other one!”

For I was thinking to myself that it is impossible for a human being to overcome a spirit or an angel of God. Rather, people fall to the ground from fear when they see them, and those who have appeared to them can barely give them strength. Such was my thought.

And look, the two quickly revealed themselves to be demons. And I realized that this was Satan’s effort to deceive the crowds gathered in places, so that they would tolerate the mysteries and the ungodliness of those who do scandalous deeds among them, until the weeds far outnumbered the good seed.
For people have chosen to please those counted among the evildoers rather than to please God.

This is how it is: one person was not expelled because of his father, because they feel ashamed before him; another because of his brother; another because of an empty desire; another because of hypocrisy and favoritism; and others because they seek the favor of those who are defiled and rejected. Everything is done for people and not for Jesus, as we have said many times in many places—not only we ourselves, but also those before us who were truly chosen by God.
Then shall we find testimony in other forms concerning cutting off from the body the limbs that have rotted in it?
Are the Scriptures not sufficient, commanding us to uproot and tear down, to build and plant?
But I have told you, brothers, that the enemy leads astray many of those who readily believe every word and every spirit.
This is what happens in many places: many fight on behalf of ungodliness because they put their trust in deceiving spirits and the teachings of demons.
Indeed, it is not an evil thing if a person who loves Christ fights with a good spirit when it appears to him.
The spirit itself loves him all the more and rejoices over him.
For it knows that he is not opposing it, but is being watchful and taking care not to bow down to a demon and come under the authority of a spirit [?], thinking that it is a holy [?] angel.
Only, even if I live in the same places with people—men and women, grown men and grown women, little boys and little girls—

even if I receive the sacrament with them, even if they receive it with me, even if I pray with them, even if they pray with me, even if I eat bread with them and they eat with me, or my hand and theirs are in this same bowl at this same table, and they dare to corrupt God's creatures with any defilement or uncleanness in this house or these houses and these places, [?] built in [?] his name with great effort and with much gold and copper and every kind of vessel—you will not acquire them all until we have put them in order—so that souls may benefit and souls may come before God in complete purity,
not only am I their enemy throughout the days of my life, as they have said many times;

even if I speak peaceful words with them, even if I act like someone rejoicing with them or blessing them, they are all the more accursed, together with all their deeds. And those who know about their deeds and cover up for them are all the more accursed along with them and all their deeds.
